stated.value: Rapeseed oil and methanol (molar ratio 6:1) converted to fatty acid methyl ester; ester phase is a clear to slightly hazy yellow liquid after R-202 and can be turbid after the wash column because of entrained water droplets until it passes the dryer (Doc p.3).

Methyl ester content 96.5 to 99.5 wt% (specification minimum 96.5 wt%), desired resolution 0.2 wt%; residual methanol 0.05 to 0.5 wt% at MP-2; water 200 to 2000 ppm depending on the point, specification limit 500 ppm in the final product (Doc p.5). Free and total glycerol are of interest but secondary (Doc p.5).

MP-1: outlet of reactor R-202, line DN80, stainless steel 1.4571. MP-2: outlet of the wash column C-301, line DN50 (target residual methanol 0.1 to 0.5 wt% and water 500 to 2000 ppm before drying). MP-3: outlet of dryer D-401, line DN50 (target water 200 to 500 ppm, limit 500 ppm according to EN 14214) (Doc p.4).
MP-1: 60 to 65 °C, 3 barg, flow 12 m³/h; MP-2: 40 to 50 °C, 2 barg; MP-3: 80 to 90 °C, 1.5 barg (Doc p.4). Dryer D-401 at 90 °C and 150 mbar; throughput 12 m³/h (Doc p.3).

All measurement points are inside an ATEX Zone 1 area because of methanol vapour; any probe and housing at the line must be certified for Zone 1 (Doc p.4). Analyzer house with purge and climate control 60 m from MP-1 and 45 m from MP-2 and MP-3, outside Zone 1 (Doc p.6). Probes must withstand cleaning with hot water at 80 °C during shutdowns; no CIP chemicals are used (Doc p.8).

Ester content by gas chromatography according to EN 14103; methanol by headspace GC according to EN 14110; water by coulometric Karl Fischer titration according to EN ISO 12937; laboratory turnaround 2 hours (Doc p.7). Existing plant-lab FTIR spectrometer with diamond ATR accessory for incoming oil checks (Doc p.6).

Replace off-line laboratory measurement every 4 hours (Doc p.2) with an in-line value at least every 2 minutes at each measurement point (Doc p.8); accuracy expectation ester within 0.3 wt%, methanol within 0.05 wt%, water within 50 ppm compared with the laboratory reference (Doc p.8).

missing: Samples with reference values from MP-1 and MP-2 (retained samples exist for MP-3 only) covering both rapeseed and used cooking oil feedstock
Which residual methanol range applies at MP-2 (0.1 to 0.5 wt% on p.4 vs 0.05 to 0.5 wt% on p.5) and the expected residual triglyceride range at MP-1
Repeatability of the laboratory reference methods compared with the requested accuracy (e.g. water within 50 ppm)

status_reason: Material, target quantities, measurement points and conditions are defined in the project document, so a provisional assessment is possible; it is not a pilot approval, because no spectra of the client's ester phase exist yet and the method must first be screened in the laboratory against the client's references. Whether one multiplexed spectrometer can serve all three points (asked on Doc p.8) can only be answered after the lab test shows which method and probe each point needs.
answer: Test NIR with transmission/transflection probes first, with the spectrometer in the analyzer house and low-OH silica fiber cables (45 to 60 m), because AFS sources state that NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and that 100 to 300 m silica cables enable remote process control. Raman (785 nm excitation) should be compared in the same lab test, and MIR ATR can be screened on the existing lab FTIR, but in-line MIR over 45 to 60 m is not covered by the AFS sources. The low water range at MP-3 (200 to 500 ppm, within 50 ppm) is the critical point that the lab test must prove.

inline.headline: Test NIR transmission/transflection probes on retained and new ester-phase samples from MP-1 to MP-3, against Raman, before any in-line pilot
inline.probe: NIR transmission/transflection probe (path 1–10 mm, to be optimised) for the clear streams at MP-1 and MP-3; transflection vs diffuse reflection to be compared for the turbid stream at MP-2
inline.install: Probes at MP-1 (R-202 outlet, DN80), MP-2 (C-301 outlet, DN50) and MP-3 (D-401 outlet, DN50); spectrometer in the purged analyzer house outside Zone 1
inline.fiber: Low-OH Vis-NIR silica fiber (350–2400 nm), 45–60 m via existing cable trays
inline.not_final_because: No spectra of the client's ester phase exist yet; NIR may lack sensitivity below about 0.1 %, while MP-3 water must be measured at 200–500 ppm within 50 ppm; the turbid MP-2 stream may need a different probe geometry; Zone 1 certification of the probes and the multiplexing scheme for a 2-minute value at each point are not yet defined.

problems.text: Water at MP-3 must be measured at 200 to 500 ppm (0.02 to 0.05 %) within 50 ppm. AFS sources note that NIR may lack sensitivity below 0.1 % (bioprocess example), and the AFS water-in-oil example only shows 0.1 to 2.0 % water, so the low ppm range is not yet covered by any example and must be proven in the lab test.

The site wants all spectrometers in the analyzer house 45 to 60 m away. AFS sources support 100 to 300 m silica cables for Vis-NIR (and Raman), but for mid-IR fibers only transmission ranges and 2 m comparisons are given, so in-line MIR ATR from the analyzer house is not supported by the sources and should be limited to lab screening for now.

MP-2 can be turbid because of entrained water droplets. NIR transmission/transflection works for transparent or semi-transparent liquids with a controlled 1 to 10 mm path, while reflection is used for opaque products; the probe geometry for MP-2 must be chosen by testing both on real turbid samples.

The project document gives two different residual methanol ranges for MP-2: 0.1 to 0.5 wt% on p.4 and 0.05 to 0.5 wt% on p.5. MP-1 also lists residual triglycerides as a target on p.4, but p.5 gives no range for them. The calibration range must be fixed before samples are selected.

All points are in ATEX Zone 1 and any probe and housing at the line must be Zone 1 certified. Passive fiber cables are accepted for Zone 1 routing, but the AFS sources contain no statement on Zone 1 certified probes, so the certification route for each probe must be clarified.

A chemometric model needs calibration samples spanning all ranges and both feedstocks (rapeseed and used cooking oil, changed about twice per month), but retained samples with reference values exist only for MP-3; samples for MP-1 and MP-2 must be collected with paired laboratory references.

methods.why: NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method, works with silica fibers that can run 100 to 300 m to an analyzer house, and covers the moisture bands at 1.3 to 2.2 µm; its overlapping bands need a chemometric model.

Raman carries information complementary to IR, AFS has measured Raman spectra of refined rapeseed oil (2600–3100 cm-1 shown), and it uses silica fibers; its signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence of organic compounds, so this must be checked on the yellow ester phase.

Mid-IR gives well-defined absorption peaks and AFS shows water-in-oil ATR spectra (4000–2000 cm-1); it can be screened on the client's existing lab FTIR with diamond ATR, but the thin ATR layer and the lack of long-fiber evidence limit it in-line.
UV-Vis has low selectivity and strongly overlapping signals in real mixtures, which does not fit separate ester, methanol and water values.
Fluorimetry relies on emission of certain, mostly biological substances; most chemicals do not fluoresce, so it gives no direct route to ester, methanol or water.

questions.q: Can the laboratory collect paired samples from MP-1 and MP-2 (and fresh MP-3 samples) with EN 14103, EN 14110 and EN ISO 12937 reference values, covering both rapeseed and used cooking oil feedstock?
questions.why: Retained samples exist only for MP-3, and the model must cover both feedstocks and all ranges.

questions.q: Which residual methanol range is valid at MP-2 (0.1 to 0.5 wt% or 0.05 to 0.5 wt%), and what residual triglyceride range is expected at MP-1?
questions.why: The document states two ranges and no triglyceride range; the calibration design depends on it.

questions.q: What is the repeatability of your Karl Fischer and GC reference results, compared with the requested accuracy (water within 50 ppm, methanol within 0.05 wt%, ester within 0.3 wt%)?
questions.why: The in-line model is judged against these laboratory references, so their own scatter limits the achievable accuracy.

questions.q: Which process connections are available at MP-1 (DN80) and MP-2/MP-3 (DN50), e.g. insertion ports, flanges or a bypass, and which Zone 1 certification documentation do you require for a probe?
questions.why: Probe type, path length and certification depend on the mounting and on the Zone 1 requirement.

questions.q: Can a sample from MP-2 be taken and kept so that its turbidity (entrained water droplets) is preserved for the lab test?
questions.why: The probe geometry for MP-2 has to be chosen on representative turbid samples.

technical.spectral_window: NIR 780–2500 nm, limited by Vis-NIR silica fiber to 350–2400 nm; moisture bands at 1.3–1.7, 1.5–2.0 and 1.7–2.2 µm. Raman: excitation 785 nm (680 nm also available), Raman shift range to be set in the lab test (rapeseed-oil spectra shown at 2600–3100 cm-1, i.e. scattered light at about 1040 nm, inside the silica range). MIR ATR lab screening at 4000–2000 cm-1 (2.5–5 µm) as in the water-in-oil example.
technical.probe: NIR transmission/transflection probe with path 1–10 mm for MP-1 and MP-3; transflection and diffuse reflection to be compared at turbid MP-2. Tip/window material unknown – ask; wetted parts must be compatible with methanol, KOH traces and glycerol and withstand hot water at 80 °C (Doc p.8). For MIR lab screening: diamond ATR (existing lab FTIR, Doc p.6).
technical.fiber: Low-OH (<0.1 ppm OH) Vis-NIR silica fiber; 60 m to MP-1 and 45 m to MP-2/MP-3 (Doc p.6), within the 100–300 m cable range; routed through existing cable trays, no fiber installed yet; passive fiber cables accepted for Zone 1 routing (Doc p.14). Exact route length unknown – ask.
technical.process_conditions: MP-1: 60–65 °C, 3 barg, 12 m³/h, DN80, stainless steel 1.4571; MP-2: 40–50 °C, 2 barg, DN50, possibly turbid; MP-3: 80–90 °C, 1.5 barg, DN50 (Doc p.3–4). Cleaning with hot water at 80 °C during shutdowns, no CIP chemicals (Doc p.8). ATEX Zone 1 at all points (Doc p.4).
technical.sampling: Three points MP-1, MP-2, MP-3; a new value at least every 2 minutes at each point; one multiplexed spectrometer for all three points is requested (Doc p.8). Output to DCS via 4–20 mA or Modbus TCP (Doc p.6).
technical.reference_method: Independent laboratory analyses: ester by GC (EN 14103), methanol by headspace GC (EN 14110), water by coulometric Karl Fischer (EN ISO 12937); turnaround 2 hours, about 6 samples per day per point (Doc p.7).
technical.calibration: Samples spanning ester 96.5–99.5 wt%, methanol 0.05–0.5 wt% (range to be confirmed) and water 200–2000 ppm (Doc p.5), from both rapeseed and used cooking oil feedstock (Doc p.3); MP-3 can start from the about 900 retained samples (Doc p.7). Build, validate on an independent sample set and then apply the model.

experiment.objective: Find out whether NIR (compared with Raman and MIR ATR) sees the differences in ester content, residual methanol and water in the client's ester phase at the three measurement points, at the client's temperatures, before deciding on a pilot.
steps: Collect samples from MP-1, MP-2 and MP-3 covering the stated ranges and both feedstocks, each with paired laboratory reference values (EN 14103, EN 14110, EN ISO 12937); include retained MP-3 samples.

Measure all samples in the AFS multi-spectral fiber lab set-up with NIR transmission/transflection (and diffuse reflection for turbid MP-2 samples), Raman at 785 nm, and MIR ATR, at the process temperatures of each point.
Use fiber lengths representative of the 45–60 m route for NIR and Raman to check signal quality in the analyzer-house configuration.
Identify key spectral features for water, methanol and ester by multivariate analysis and compare which method separates the levels.
Build calibration models per method and point, validate them on an independent sample set against the laboratory references, and test NIR + Raman fusion on the same validation data.
Report achievable accuracy per point against the client's targets and propose probe geometry, multiplexing and the next step (pilot or not).
references: Ester content: GC according to EN 14103
Methanol: headspace GC according to EN 14110
Water: coulometric Karl Fischer titration according to EN ISO 12937
experiment.go_no_go: Client criteria (Doc p.8): ester within 0.3 wt%, methanol within 0.05 wt%, water within 50 ppm compared with the laboratory reference, and a new value at least every 2 minutes at each measurement point.

pathway.key_features: Not yet available: no spectra of the client's ester phase have been supplied. Candidate regions to check are the NIR moisture bands (1.3–2.2 µm), the Raman spectrum of rapeseed oil (2600–3100 cm-1 shown) and the MIR water-in-oil region 4000–2000 cm-1.
pathway.path_reason: Key spectral features and a validated model must come from the multi-method lab test first.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups (water, methanol O-H), while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups (ester chain), so the information is complementary; both run on silica fibers and can share the analyzer-house location.
multispectral.probe: Separate synchronised probes at the clear points MP-1 and MP-3; at the turbid MP-2 a combined probe seeing the same spot is preferable because heterogeneous samples need the same small area.
multispectral.fusion: Low-level fusion of synchronised spectra with PLS, using dedicated data-fusion algorithms because the blocks differ in noise and information content.
multispectral.test: Build NIR-only, Raman-only and fused models on the same calibration samples and compare them on the same independent validation set against the laboratory references; the combination is only kept if it beats the best single method.

assumptions: The stream at MP-3 is clear, since the document says it is turbid only until it passes the dryer (Doc p.3).
The fiber route length is close to the stated 45–60 m distances; the real tray route may be longer.
The temperatures stated per point stay within the given ranges during the lab test and in operation.
